findings.evidence: `rg` shows the adjacent product API keeps the additive bridge private (`ElementaryTwoQuotientProd.lean:100`, `:163`) and exposes the linear equivalence without `@[expose]` (`:117`, `:181`).
findings.fix: Make the range theorem and additive equivalence private, remove `@[expose]` from the linear equivalence, and expose only characteristic lemmas needed by users.
findings.issue: The public surface leaks implementation helpers: `range_lsmul_two_additive_multiplicative_zmod_two_toAddSubgroup_eq_bot` and the additive bridge at line 70 are only used to build the linear equivalence, and both equivalence bodies are marked `@[expose]` despite consumers using the mk/card/rank API.

findings.evidence: The file provides `elementaryTwoQuotientMultiplicativeZModTwoLinearEquiv_mk` at lines 89-105, while the parallel product/pi APIs include both forward and inverse simp lemmas (`ElementaryTwoQuotientProd.lean:123-136`, `:186-198`).
findings.fix: Add a `[simp]` inverse formula, e.g. `(elementaryTwoQuotientMultiplicativeZModTwoLinearEquiv).symm z = elementaryTwoQuotientMk (Multiplicative.ofAdd z)`.
findings.issue: The linear equivalence has only the forward representative formula; users cannot simplify the inverse map without unfolding the definition.

summary: The new computation exposes quotient-model construction details and leaves the main equivalence without the inverse characteristic lemma used by adjacent API.
